ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows a gray cube with circular/hemispherical depressions centered on the visible faces: top, front, and right. These visible holes illustrate that holes on neighboring perpendicular faces are the ones that touch. Reasoning: Model the cube of side length 2 with coordinates from -1 to 1 in each direction. The centers of two adjacent face holes can be taken as the centers of the faces x=1 and y=1, namely (1,0,0) and (0,1,0). The distance between these adjacent face centers is sqrt((1-0)^2 + (0-1)^2 + (0-0)^2) = sqrt(2). Since the hemispherical holes are identical and just touch neighboring holes, the corresponding full spheres would be tangent, so their center distance equals 2r. Thus 2r = sqrt(2). The diameter of each hole is therefore sqrt(2).

method.method_draft: Take a 2D cross-section through the centers of two neighbouring holes and parallel to the line joining those face centers. From the image, neighbouring holes lie on adjacent faces; in such a cross-section of the cube, the relevant part is a square of side 2 with two semicircular cutouts centered at the midpoints of adjacent sides. The distance between adjacent side midpoints of a 2-by-2 square is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 1 and 1, so it is sqrt(2). Since the semicircular cross-sections of the two hemispheres just touch, the sum of their equal radii equals this distance, so the diameter, 2r, is sqrt(2).
